claims.explanation: PHA-665752 is a potent and selective c-Met kinase inhibitor, and its antiproliferative activity is strongly associated with c-Met dependency, most clearly seen in cancers with MET gene amplification or high MET expression. The most sensitive lines include gastric and other cancers known to harbor MET amplification, while resistant lines often lack MET activation or have mutations in downstream effectors that bypass c-Met signaling. Thus, MET amplification/overexpression and possibly activating MET mutations are the primary sensitizing features, whereas mutations in PI3K pathway components or RAS/RAF may confer resistance.

features.basis: High MET expression/amplification drives oncogene addiction and sensitivity to c-Met inhibitors
Activating MET mutations can confer sensitivity to c-Met inhibitors
PI3K pathway mutations may bypass c-Met dependence and reduce sensitivity
RAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling independent of c-Met
BRAF mutations drive MAPK pathway activation bypassing c-Met
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling independent of c-Met
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK pathway bypassing c-Met
EGFR mutations may provide alternative survival signaling
ERBB3 mutations can activate PI3K/AKT independent of c-Met
KIT mutations may drive alternative RTK signaling
